text:
rachel: Noticed an odd pattern in offload logs: asymmetric host->gpu copies during mixed-size allocations. Small slots are being offloaded eagerly while adjacent medium slots stay resident, creating fragmentation and unnecessary PCIe churn.

marc: that's the asymmetry we discussed months ago. Any correlation with the new offload-window code?

irvan: fwiw the offload-window heuristic currently treats slots <256B as immediate candidates when host_free_percent < 20%. That was to protect large tensors, but it can make hot small-scratch buffers bounce if their neighbors are medium and pinned.

emily: can you paste the trace?

rachel: trace excerpt:
```
[t=12:01:02] slot#204 size=64 state=host-queued
[t=12:01:02] slot#205 size=16384 state=gpu-resident pinned=1
[t=12:01:03] slot#204 offloaded -> gpu (copy 64B)
[t=12:01:03] slot#206 size=64 alloc -> host
[t=12:01:03] slot#204 evicted -> host (shortly after)
```
Seeing repeated small copies next to large pinned slots.

marc: sounds like our neighbor-awareness is too binary. Maybe introduce a locality score that reasons about slot-group homogeneity. If a slot's neighbors are heterogenous (large pinned), raise the offload threshold to avoid bouncing.

irvan: agree. propose: offload_score = base_score - neighbor_penalty, where neighbor_penalty = sum(size_weight * pinned_flag) across k neighbors. If offload_score < threshold, defer to recluster or add to delayed queue.

emily: deferring might increase host memory but reduce PCIe thrash. We need a cost model: cost_offload = pcie_latency + copy_cost - benefit (future hits saved). Can we estimate benefit from recent access frequency?

rachel: we have per-slot access counters (8-sample ring). Use that to estimate future hit probability. For small scratch with low freq, benefit small. So combine freq with neighbor_penalty into decision.

marc: implementation surface: update offload policy module to expose hooks: compute_offload_score(slot_id) and schedule_offload(slot_id, policy_flags). We'll add a delayed_offload queue with priorities and backoff.

irvan: locking: scheduling an offload must observe slot->state transitions. Use CAS to move host->delayed_offload and record backoff_deadline. Worker threads poll delayed queue and respect GPU util/pci budget.

emily: perf-bot, can we get a simulated run with current heuristic vs neighbor-aware heuristic on the replay harness?

perf-bot: scheduled: replay job #8821 queued. Will run A/B with 1h traces from pool-D. Results expected in ~2h.

marc: telemetry additions: offload_deferrals, neighbor_penalty_histogram, delayed_queue_length, offload_retries, pci_bandwidth_saved_estimate. Also add a gauge for offload_worker_lag.

rachel: risk: delayed offloads can increase host RSS and cause false OOM windows under spikey workloads. Mitigation: make delayed queue size-bounded and add emergency drain that triggers when host_rss > host_rss_limit - margin. Drain must prefer low neighbor_penalty slots.

irvan: another corner: recluster may want to compact medium slots but if we delay offload it might block recluster progress. Need coordination: recluster should peek at delayed queue and escalate slots eligible for compaction.

emily: propose an escalation policy: if slot has been delayed > T_escalate or delayed_count > N, mark for recluster_hint. Then recluster can attempt to move hot ones or coalesce cold ones.

marc: rollout: feature-flag neighbor-aware offload. Canary on 5% nodes for 24h, monitor pci_util, host_rss, and offload_retries. If pci_util drops and p99 latency unchanged, expand.

rachel: perf-bot will post A/B results. If good, I'll draft an RFC describing the scoring function, delayed queue semantics, and escalator pseudocode. Include microbench numbers: expected pci bandwidth saved and projected host memory increase.

emily: one more thought: for tenant-isolated pools we may want to disable neighbor_penalty to avoid penalizing tenants with heavy pinned workloads. Add per-pool config: neighbor_aware = on/off.

perf-bot: replay job #8821 complete: neighbor-aware reduced offload_count by 28% and estimated PCIe bytes by 34% on trace; host_rss increased by 90MB peak (within margin). No p99 latency regression observed.

marc: nice. go ahead with RFC. I'll review lock-order and CAS pseudocode.

rachel: thanks all. RFC link when ready.
